title: Indicator v2
description: A source-specific operationalisation of a construct: a measured quantity observed for a site, area, country, or grid cell. unit describes the measurement scale and is distinct from the unit of analysis. A ratio indicator uses unit rate and identifies its denominator through denominator_indicator_id. construct_id identifies the construct in the consuming product's vocabulary; indicators of the same construct retain their separate identities.

unit.description: Measurement unit. index denotes an index score whose scale and construction are documented in method; percent_point denotes a difference between percentages. These additions were approved 2026-09-11. Changes to this vocabulary require a new versioned schema.

construct_id.description: Construct this indicator operationalises, identified in the consuming product's construct vocabulary. Omit or use null for legacy indicators awaiting a construct assignment; validation against the vocabulary is a consumer responsibility.

variable_kind.description: Classification of the measure: intensive for quantities such as rates, means, and indices; extensive for additive quantities such as counts over disjoint units; code for categorical values. Valid aggregation depends on the indicator-specific method, denominator, weights, and target units. A weighted mean or apportioned sum requires justification for that indicator and intended aggregation. Categorical codes identify categories.

native_period_type.description: The source's own period concept for a value: a calendar year, a survey fieldwork span, a pooled multi-year estimate, or a single reference date.

method.description: How the value was derived or transcribed. Document the scale, denominator, and any aggregation method and weights needed to interpret or combine values.

$comment: Supersedes indicator.schema.json for consumers that opt into the closed measurement-unit contract. The original unversioned schema remains available unchanged for legacy consumers. Adopted 2026-09-11; see schemas/README.md for migration and supersession rules.
